patch_description: The current candidate added a final global RY layer that reuses "theta_ry" as a post-entangling "output mixer" at zero extra parameter cost. Empirically this hurt performance: the current program scores 0.57 (validation accuracy 0.88) versus the earlier 2-parameter multi-shell candidate without this mixer layer, which scored 0.61 (validation accuracy 0.90). Reusing theta_ry for both the initial state-preparation rotation and a final pre-measurement rotation couples two roles that want different optimal angles under gradient descent, since the parameter is shared identically across all 3 repeated blocks and now also across both intra-block sub-roles -- this likely creates conflicting gradients that slow/impair convergence (worst_group_margin also dropped from 0.35/0.33 baseline). Removing the redundant output-mixer layer reverts to the simpler, empirically stronger 2-parameter structure (theta_ry local rotation + theta_z shared across RZ layer and all three CRZ entangling shells), restoring the higher validation accuracy and margin while keeping the same minimal parameter count.
